speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the nature of the swelling and pain, and how long have you been experiencing these symptoms?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds like a traumatic injury; did the pain start immediately upon impact, or did it develop gradually over those two days? I also need to know if you noticed any deformity, such as the finger looking crooked or the joint appearing out of place.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Progressive swelling and pain in the right ring finger. I also have Inability to flex the right ring finger at the distal interphalangeal joint when making a fist, Pain at the distal interphalangeal joint, Extended right ring finger in resting position.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Mallet Finger (distal interphalangeal joint extensor tendon rupture).

Please proceed with the standard treatment protocol for a mallet finger, which typically involves immobilization with a finger splint in extension. Do you have any difficulty extending the fingertip or any numbness in the finger?

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
